newsitem.title: UK: Most Britons against single Euro currency -survey.
newsitem.headline: Most Britons against single Euro currency -survey.

text.p: A majority of Britons do not want to give up sterling in favour of a single European currency, according to a poll published on Wednesday.
The MORI poll, which will appear in this week's European newspaper, found that 64 percent of Britons said they would vote against the single currency if a referendum were held now.
And 40 percent would vote to pull out of the European Union altogether, with only a slim majority of 44 percent continuing to support membership. The rest were undecided.

An overwhelming majority of 85 percent was in favour of the 48-hour working week set out in a European directive. The British government opposed the directive but lost in an appeal to the European Court of Justice last month.
MORI questioned 1,025 people in 65 constituencies around Britain between November 27 and 29.
